statusFinding.explanation: There is NO selective licensing designation in force in Redcar and Cleveland on 7 August 2026. The council's own signed designation notice, still hosted on redcar-cleveland.gov.uk at https://www.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2022-04/Signed%20Notice%20-%20Designation%20of%20an%20area%20for%20Selective%20Licensing.pdf and headed 'REDCAR & CLEVELAND BOROUGH COUNCIL - DESIGNATION OF AN AREA FOR SELECTIVE LICENSING (SOUTH BANK) 2019, Housing Act 2004 - Section 80', states in terms: 'The designation was made on 20 December 2018 and comes into force on 25 March 2019. The designation will have effect until 24 March 2024.' It is dated 20 December 2018 and signed by Patrick Rice, Director of Adults & Communities. That end date, 24 March 2024, has passed and no successor designation could be found on any official council source. Corroborating evidence that no scheme survives: (1) the council's selective licensing page at https://www.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk/housing/housing-standards/selective-licensing now returns a Drupal 'Access denied - Sorry, you do not have access to this page' response, i.e. the node has been unpublished, not merely moved; (2) the word 'selective' appears zero times across all 871 URLs in the council's live sitemap at https://www.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk/sitemap.xml, which does still list eleven other Housing Standards pages including the HMO licensing page - so this is an absence, not a crawl failure; (3) the Housing Standards index at https://www.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk/housing/housing-standards returns HTTP 200 and lists its ten child pages (Renters' Rights Act 2025, Housing issues and standards, Empty Homes, Energy efficiency, House in multiple occupancy, Tenant and landlord relations, Pest control, Statutory nuisance, Boiler Upgrade Scheme, Warm Homes Local Grant) with selective licensing absent; (4) the former application portal at selectivelicensing.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk no longer serves a response. This is a textbook example of the Sheffield pattern and is why the previous record was wrong: the council left the 'apply for a selective licence' page and its live application portal up for well over a year after the designation lapsed. A Wayback capture of the council's own page taken on 29 April 2025 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250429222800/https://www.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk/housing/housing-standards/selective-licensing) still invited landlords to 'Submit a selective licence application' while its own body text read 'South Bank was designated for Selective Licensing in 2018. The designation will have effect until 24 March 2024' - a live portal advertising an already-expired scheme. As to a replacement: a full council motion carried in January 2026 asked cabinet to direct officers to establish whether there is evidence to justify a new scheme in the Brotton, Eston and Normanby wards. That is an instruction to gather evidence only. No designation notice, no consultation outcome and no start date for an East Cleveland scheme exists on any official council source, so it remains PROPOSED and must not be treated as live. Separately, note that the previous record's start date of 25 March 2019 was correct but its implied designation date was not: the designation was MADE on 20 December 2018 (hence the council's page describing South Bank as 'designated for Selective Licensing in 2018') and came into FORCE on 25 March 2019.

schemes.evidence: No street list exists to transcribe, and none ever did. The 'Designation of an Area for Selective Licensing (South Bank) 2019' was not street-based: the council's signed s.83 notice defines the area only as 'South Bank (older housing area)', stating it is 'more particularly detailed on a plan available for inspection at all reasonable hours' at Redcar & Cleveland Borough Council, Kirkleatham Street, Redcar, TS10 1RT. That plan was never published online; it was inspection-only at the council offices. No schedule of designated streets appears in the notice, on the council's former selective licensing page (checked via the 29 April 2025 Wayback capture of the official page, which listed only the designation notice under 'Related Links'), or anywhere in the council's 871-URL sitemap. Marked not-found rather than fabricated. In any case the designation expired on 24 March 2024, so no street list is operationally required - see statusFinding. Any street-level list for Redcar and Cleveland circulating on commercial sites (legislate.tech, propertylicence.org.uk and similar) is not derived from any published council source and should not be trusted.
